newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo cracks down on teenage prostitution 'clubs'.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo cracks down on teenage prostitution 'clubs'.

text.p: Tokyo on Wednesday introduced stiff measures to combat a rising trend of teenage girls selling sex to older men through so-called telephone date clubs, a spokesman for the Tokyo metropolitan government said.

"As of today it will be illegal to put up posters and fliers advertising the clubs within 200 metres (yards) of schools and illegal for any such establishment to let girls under 18 inside," said a spokesman for Tokyo's Youth Division.
"We will be imposing this law very strictly and will no doubt be conducting raids on telephone clubs in the near future," the spokesman added.
A survey by the Tokyo government last year found that about a quarter of female students aged from 12 to 15 years had taken part in the telephone chat clubs.

Male clients of telephone clubs pay to enter booths in the club and wait for private calls from women and girls, who dial a free telephone number from outside the club, often from their own home or a public telephone box.
The phone conversations usually fix a date to meet and are often a straightforward agreement on the details and price of the particular sexual act to be performed, the spokesman said.
He added that the Tokyo government is likely to step up the fight against teenage prostitution by passing a law in September to punish adults who buy sex from minors under eighteen years old.
"Up until now there has been no punishment for the clients of prostitutes. We hope the new law will work as a stronger deterrent," he said.
The legal age of consent for sex in Tokyo and Nagano Prefecture is 13, compared with 18 in the rest of the country, he said.
Telephone clubs have flourished in Japan in recent years, amid a general climate of growing interest in extramarital affairs by both men and women and in prostitution by teenage girls.
Younger girls fetch a premium from "lolicon" clients, older men with "Lolita complexes" toward little girls.
Japanese media reports quote teenage prostitutes as saying they have sex for money, mainly with middle-aged men, so they can afford expensive brand-name clothes and accessories.
A 1996 National Police Agency survey showed that teenagers selling sex rose to one-third of all reported cases of prostitution.
The survey also reported that, for the first time, the number of girls engaging in prostitution for money had exceeded those who did it for excitement.
Activist groups have called for a ban on child pornography, which is legal in Japan, and strict punishment of customers of child prostitutes.
